records.note: no New Hampshire-specific prison-housing data found: the mandated single enwiki full-text search (New Hampshire transgender prisoner housing solitary) returned only generic US pages (Transgender rights in the United States; LGBTQ people in prison); both candidate fetches returned HTTP 200 and were read in full, and New Hampshire appears in them only for gender-marker availability, anti-discrimination statutes (2018), youth gender-affirming-care bans (2024/2025) and sports bans — never for trans-prisoner placement. The fetched pages document US federal/US-wide practice only: a January 2017 Obama-era Bureau of Prisons guidance allowing transgender prisoners to be transferred to and housed in facilities matching their gender identity, rescinded on 11 May 2018 so that assigned sex at birth again determined placement; the February 2025 New York Times-reported federal ruling blocking the administration's effort to move transgender women to men's prisons; and documented V-coding/solitary-confinement practice against trans women in men's facilities. No New Hampshire Department of Corrections placement rule (birth-sex vs identity), trans special unit, or state solitary/segregation practice or ruling was located within the fetch budget; no usable jurisdiction finding.
